title: Hubiera Without Si, and Even If in the Past

sections.title: Two more uses of hubiera
sections.content: You know *si hubiera tenido* from B1 Unit 35, and *aun cuando* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 8. This lesson adds two ways to use the pluperfect subjunctive. First, you can drop *si* and put *hubiera* + past participle at the start of the sentence: *Hubiera salido antes, habría llegado*. It means the same as the sentence with *si*, and it sounds more emphatic. Second, *aun cuando* or *aunque* + *hubiera* + participle says "even if … had …": the result would have been the same: *Aun cuando hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos llegado*.

sections.title: Two patterns
rows: Had I left earlier, I would have arrived. (= Si hubiera salido antes…)
Had we left earlier, we would have arrived.
Aun cuando hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos llegado.
Even if we had left earlier, we would not have arrived.
Aunque hubiera estudiado toda la noche, no habría aprobado.
Even if I had studied all night, I would not have passed.

items.spanish: Hubiera sabido la verdad, habría actuado de otra manera.
items.english: Had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.

items.spanish: Hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos llegado a tiempo.
items.english: Had we left earlier, we would have arrived on time.

items.spanish: Aun cuando hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos llegado a tiempo.
items.english: Even if we had left earlier, we would not have arrived on time.

sections.content: Only *hubiera* + participle can start a sentence without *si*, and only with a comma before the result. After *aun cuando* and *aunque* keep the pluperfect subjunctive in the first clause and the conditional perfect (or *hubiera* + participle) in the result.
